notes: Sixth full sweep (2026-10-23, head d04061d, uncommitted false), baseline condition of log-tests: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript shows a Read of the input and a Write of the test file followed by elixir -r runs; opus-1 also read the ExUnit.CaptureLog docs with Code.fetch_docs before writing, and opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 ran mutant checks of their own. No Skill tool call; reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. No session ran mix format, yet all five files pass mix format --check-formatted, matching format_ok in result.json.

Rules changed since ba24972 (git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/): SKILL.md rewrote "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" and added three paragraphs to "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys"; ex_unit.md added one sentence to "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" ("A crash report's content depends on the primary level alone: ..."). That sentence concerns crash reports, which this case does not produce, so it decides no verdict; the capture_log rule is graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard on its unchanged sentences. "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state", "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", "Assert with patterns" and "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard.

Per-sentence counts for the rewritten rules (both outside this case's list, so they only feed other_violations; the bullet-per-sentence lists the caller mentioned are in webhook-parser.md and library-client.md, not in log-tests.md). "Read required keys ...": first sentence (required keys with map[:key]) 1 of 5 (sonnet-1, lines 94-95 and 108-109, unchanged sentence); the new pattern-as-dot-access sentence ("A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long") 0 of 5; the chain sentence 0 of 5 (every run reads event.meta.request_id as one chain); the Map.fetch sentence not exercised. "In multi-clause functions ...": 0 of 5 on every sentence. The only multi-clause functions are haiku-1's message/1 (lines 48-50) and haiku-2's message_text/1 (lines 118-120), whose heads match a tagged tuple and bind its elements; those are tuple elements of the selecting pattern, not fields the body could read with dot access, so the field sentence does not apply. No head pattern moved into a body, and no string-keyed parser.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler": 4 of 5 violate (5 of 5 in 2026-10-22-d). opus-1 is the first baseline run in this case to keep the rule: after reading the CaptureLog docs it wraps every call in with_log/2 with :format and :metadata options (lines 33-38) and asserts anchored lines on the captured text. haiku-1 (lines 32-35), haiku-2 (line 33), sonnet-1 (lines 43-47, with Logger.configure at line 41) and sonnet-2 (line 35) add a :logger handler that sends events to the test process and assert on the event maps. Calls outside a capture: none in opus-1 (with_log) or haiku-2 (@moduletag capture_log: true); every charge/3 call in haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, whose runs print 8, 6 and 4 log lines.

To check the log assertions are not vacuous, each file was run against the five mutants of the earlier sweeps (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error). Every file fails at least one test on every mutant, opus-1's capture-based file included (2/3, 2/3, 2/3, 0/3, 2/3 passed).

"Assert with patterns": 4 of 5 violate with the shape of 2026-10-22-d, binding a log event and then comparing its fields with == (haiku-1 lines 92-96, haiku-2 lines 51-53, sonnet-1 lines 93-95, sonnet-2 lines 64-67). Judgment, as before: the bound value comes from the test's own drain helper, not from charge/3, and is graded under the rule's first example. opus-1 is clean: {result, log} = with_log(...) is the exempted destructure, and assert result == {:ok, "ch_123"} compares the whole value with the value under test on the left. Bound collections compared with == [] (haiku-1 line 72, haiku-1 line 103, sonnet-1 line 81) put the value under test on the left and are not violations.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 3 of 5 violate (4 of 5 in 2026-10-22-d). haiku-2 (fixed handler id, line 27) and sonnet-1 (Logger.configure, line 41) force async: false with their own global state, graded violated as before. haiku-1 uses a unique handler id per test (line 30) but no pid filter, so nothing outside the test forces its async: false; graded violated like 2026-10-22-d's unneeded async: false. opus-1 (no handler) and sonnet-2 (per-test handler, pid filter at line 44) are clean with async: true. The Opus tier moves from violated to clean.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": 0 of 5 violate. opus-1 has no describe block, which the rule does not forbid, so it misses the case's describe check but is graded clean on its names. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 name blocks after conditions; sonnet-2 uses "charge/3 when ...". The tersest names, haiku-2 lines 40 and 58 "returns the error" and haiku-1 line 85 "returns the decline", sit under a describe naming the condition and are graded clean as 2026-10-22-d graded "returns the gateway's error". "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5: opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one module per outcome, haiku-1 one module answering by token, haiku-2 one module whose answer each test puts in the process dictionary (not runtime patching).

Rules outside the list: "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" in 4 of 5 (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), under the sentence "That holds whether the result is passed on, matched against, nested in another call or discarded", unchanged since ba24972; the pipeline rule in haiku-1 (lines 68-70) and haiku-2 (line 120); the required-keys rule in sonnet-1. Not reported, as before: comments above handler modules (haiku-2 lines 16-17, sonnet-1 lines 5-6) and helpers (haiku-2 lines 98 and 105), as 2026-10-22-d left such comments unreported, gateway modules without @moduledoc false in an .exs script, opus-1's formatter wrap after =~ (lines 62-63), and haiku-2's 1_000 ms assert_receive timeout (line 100).

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each with random seeds. Every file passed every time with no compiler warnings: opus-1 3 tests, haiku-1 8, haiku-2 6, sonnet-1 6, sonnet-2 4. mix format --check-formatted passes for all five.
